article: Windowsで大きなフォルダーをコマンドで削除する方法と注意点
scope: Compared the complete Japanese article and all twelve translations, including every CMD command, option, quoted path, execution order, warning, title/description, and official reference.
findings: Removed the duplicate future date and retained 2022-09-20 as the publication date; set lastmod to 2026-11-24.
Corrected the instructions to run from the parent directory, inspect the target with dir /a, and quote paths containing spaces.
Explained the actual DEL /F /Q /S and RMDIR /S /Q effects, including recursive files, read-only files, no confirmation, and whole-tree removal.
Added an explicit warning to back up data and verify the target because these commands may cause irreversible data loss.
Removed the unsupported claim that deletion is always dramatically faster; performance varies and was not benchmarked.

post/大きなフォルダーを高速一括削除/index.en.md.source: post/大きなフォルダーを高速一括削除/index.md
post/大きなフォルダーを高速一括削除/index.en.md.summary: Compared the complete Japanese article and twelve translations with Microsoft command references; corrected command syntax and recursive/quiet behavior, removed an unsupported speed claim, and added path verification, backup, and irreversible-deletion warnings.

meaning.note: Compared the workflow and explained that DEL removes files recursively while RMDIR /S removes the directory tree; corrected the claim that traversal and deletion happen simultaneously and removed the unsupported guaranteed-speed claim.

terminology.note: Checked Command Prompt, parent directory, DEL, RMDIR, read-only files, recursive deletion, quiet mode, hidden/system listing, and command switches across every language.

mathematics.note: This Windows command guide contains no mathematical formulas or calculations.

code.note: Checked the exact CMD sequence: cd /d changes drive and directory; dir /a lists all target entries; DEL /F /Q /S with a quoted wildcard deletes files recursively; RMDIR /S /Q deletes the tree without confirmation. Quoting and parent-directory context were retained.

links.note: Added and checked the Microsoft Learn DEL and RMDIR references for syntax, switch behavior, irrecoverability warning, and quiet recursive directory deletion.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
Commands were checked against Microsoft documentation but were not run against a Windows directory; examples must be adapted and verified by the reader.
Deletion speed depends on file count, storage, and system conditions; no performance benchmark was performed.
